'''''Phalaris angusta''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common names '''timothy canarygrass''' and '''narrow canarygrass'''. It is native to the Americas, where it is most common in [[Chile]] and [[Argentina]] and can be found in northern South America and sections of the southwestern and southeastern United States. It is also known as an [[introduced species]] in [[Australia]].<ref>[http://pngplants.org/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Phalaris~angusta New South Wales Flora]</ref> It grows in grassland, prairie, marshland, and other habitat.

==Description==
''Phalaris angusta'' is an annual grass reaching as much as 2.5 meters tall. The [[inflorescence]] is a narrow cylindrical spike of rough-haired, pointed spikelets.

===Toxicity===
Like some other ''[[Phalaris (plant)|Phalaris]]'' species, this grass is [[Toxicity|toxic]] to [[livestock]]. Calves that eat the grass develop [[Neurology|neurological]] signs such as [[tremor]]s and [[convulsion]]s and gross examination of their brain tissue reveals large blue-green lesions.<ref>Sousa, R. S. & L. F. Irigoyen. (1999). [http://www.scielo.br/pdf/pvb/v19n3-4/0882.pdf Experimental poisoning by ''Phalaris angusta'' (Gramineae) in cattle.] ''Pesquisa Veterinária Brasileira'' 19 116-22. (Portuguese)</ref> Some cattle and sheep die suddenly after grazing in pastures of the grass, while some linger with signs of neurological compromise.<ref>Odriozola, E., et al. (1991). Neuropathological effects and deaths of cattle and sheep in Argentina from ''Phalaris angusta''. ''Veterinary and Human Toxicology'' 43:5 465-7.</ref>
